name: Interactive System Map Web Page
description: A web-page skill for turning architecture evidence into a navigable system map with editable nodes, directed relationships, semantic states, and inspectable citations. Designed for teaching, research, design review, and durable engineering documentation.
whatYouGet: A responsive dark-grid system map with stable, editable component nodes
Interactive selection, path highlighting, layer filtering, and evidence-aware details
A clear legend for verified, inferred, warning, and unresolved relationships
Technical copy explaining flow, ownership, boundaries, and failure modes
A self-contained deliverable adaptable to HTML, React, Vue, or Tailwind
goodFit: Explaining a request path across services, queues, stores, and external actors
Teaching a technical audience how a system behaves and where evidence comes from
notFor: Decorative diagrams with no source data or explanatory objective
Large-scale graph analysis needing automatic layout and query tooling
requiredInputs: A component inventory with stable names and responsibilities
Directed relationships, layers, and the primary path to explain
Evidence references, confidence levels, or explicit unknowns
Audience and teaching objective for the page

faq.a: Yes. Store confidence and evidence with the map data, then expose them through text labels, the legend, and the selected-node detail panel rather than color alone.

faq.q: How should a very large system be handled?
faq.a: Choose one primary scenario, focus the initial view on its critical path, and expose secondary domains through working layer controls.

faq.q: Can users edit the resulting map?
faq.a: Yes. Keep map data separate from rendering so labels, edges, annotations, confidence, and citations can be updated without rewriting layout code.

demoPrompt: /sl-interactive-system-map-web-page Build a Signal Blueprint-style Aster Archive page for analysts tracing document flow. In order: navigation with “Open map”; hero “Aster Archive system map” and “Explore map”; four map-control guides; selected Indexer details; four document-path steps; four inventory stats; evidence register; reading FAQ; footer links. Cover runtime and failure layers, citations, and open questions. Keep it crisp and technical.
followUpPrompts: Add a failure layer for retries, dead-letter handling, and data-loss boundaries.
Port the map to a reusable React component while preserving keyboard navigation and evidence labels.
externalCostNote: No external services. Runs entirely on your agent.
